title: istriu
summary: Determine whether a matrix is upper triangular in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs and evaluates the upper-triangular predicate on the host.

description: `istriu(A)` returns true when every element below the main diagonal of matrix `A` is zero.
behaviors: Diagonal and all-zero matrices are upper triangular.
Dense real, logical, complex, sparse, and gpuArray inputs are supported.
Complex entries count as nonzero when either real or imaginary part is nonzero.
NaN values count as nonzero when testing matrix structure.
Arrays with a non-singleton dimension beyond the second return `false`, matching MATLAB matrix-predicate behavior.

examples.description: Detecting a value below the main diagonal

faqs.question: What entries does `istriu` inspect?
faqs.answer: Only entries below the main diagonal can make the predicate false.

faqs.question: Are diagonal matrices upper triangular?
faqs.answer: Yes. Diagonal matrices have zeros below the main diagonal, so `istriu` returns true.

faqs.question: How are sparse matrices handled?
faqs.answer: RunMat scans stored sparse entries without densifying and returns false only when a stored nonzero appears below the main diagonal.

gpu_residency: RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs to host memory for this scalar predicate and returns a host logical scalar.
gpu_behavior: `istriu` is registered as a structure-analysis fusion sink. GPU-resident inputs are gathered transparently before the host predicate runs, so explicit `gather` calls are optional.
